messages:
nina: FYI - small APAC rack hit a sudden NIC tx backlog during peak training window. We saw dedicated slices moved off a handful of hosts and a few tenants started hitting cross-region fallbacks.
tom: saw the spike. NIC drop-counts + interface queue growth on rack-7. That forced our allocator to eject fractional slices to maintain host safety.
rachel: any GPU-level thermal throttles? or purely network backpressure? KV cache churn would explain slow tails.
nina: primarily network. No thermal events in host telemetry. But once slices moved, their KV caches evicted and cold RPCs climbed. Tail latency up ~280-400ms for some LLM routes.
infra-bot: alert-bot: Network backlog alert (rack-7) fired 2025-01-12T03:04:12Z - egress packets queued > 600ms.
cory: If allocator treats nic_backpressure as critical, it ends up reshuffling many frac slices; that fragmentation is what causes the cross-AZ fallbacks. Can we treat NIC warnings as degraded but not eviction-critical for dedicated pools?
tom: we currently have nic_safety=evict in the agent config. Changing to nic_safety=prefer_migrate might keep slices but route traffic slower locally.
alex: prefer slower local vs fast cross-region is cheaper and safer for QoE/cost. Proposal: set nic_safety=prefer_migrate for pools with tag:dedsafe=true for 1h canary.
rachel: also suggest a short-lived warm-reserve: when we detect >15% slice movement, create a small local warm-pool (5% of committed) pinned to same AZ for 20m to absorb KV warmups.
nina: agreed. Immediate steps Ill take: 1) flip nic_safety on dedsafe canary pools 2) trigger warm-reserve job 3) reduce router.cross_region_threshold from 0.6 -> 0.2 for dedicated tenant traffic.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: nic_safety toggle rolled to canary pools at 03:12 UTC.
tom: rolling config now. Watch for any increase in local queueing. We might see small latency rise but should cut egress costs.
rachel: runbook note: ensure cache-hint header set on moved slices so the router/ingester can prefetch state: header: X-KV-Warmup: prefer.
cory: long-term: we should add a 'network-hold' policy that prefers intra-AZ degradation over cross-AZ fallback for any reserved/dedicated slices. That can be an auto-policy on noisy racks.
alex: Billing impact: early estimate — last night cross-AZ fallbacks added ~0.09 USD / 1k tokens on affected tenants. Add to billing-events so finance can reconcile.
nina: I'll open PR for post-incident telemetry tags and cost label: router.fallback_reason=network-hold.
infra-bot: monitor-bot: billing-event logged tenant:vision-embed +0.09USD/1k tokens anomaly at 03:18Z.
tom: if this stabilizes, we can keep nic_safety change for 24h then revert. If fragmentation persists, we may consider AZ-locked dedicated assignment for very latency-sensitive tenants.
rachel: small runbook snippet for oncall:

``
On NIC-backpressure in APAC rack:
 1) set nic_safety=prefer_migrate for tag:dedsafe canaries
 2) spawn warm-reserve (5% capacity) pinned to host AZ for 20m
 3) set router.cross_region_threshold=0.2 for dedicated routes
 4) annotate billing event: router.fallback_reason=network-hold
``

alex: PR opened: internal/infra/runbooks/network-hold-2025 (https://internal/repo/runbooks/network-hold-2025) - pinged #oncall.
cory: also echo: add metric dim fallback.vs.local to the billing-export so chargeback teams can see when fallbacks happen.
nina: thanks all. I'll keep an eye and post a short postmortem if we hit >15% egress bump again. :rocket:
